detail.body:
## Summary
Every batch now records the platform it ran on, on every node: server and BIOS, CPUs, memory, GPU settings, host GPU driver and NICs. It also states it in one sentence, the form performance results are quoted with:
> Dual AMD EPYC 9575F 64-Core Processor-based Supermicro AS -4126GS-NMR-LCC server with 8x AMD Instinct MI355X (288GB HBM3E 1400W) GPUs, 1 NUMA node per socket, System BIOS 1.7, Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, Host GPU driver amdgpu 30.10.1 (ROCm 7.0.1)
It also fixes two throughput numbers the extractor got wrong. TorchTitan TFLOP/s at or above 1,000 were read as 1. Megatron-Bridge's post-training estimate was reported as TFLOP/s.
### Platform (`lib/common.sh`, `run_batch.sh`, `run_batch_multinode.sh`)
- Collected on every node without root, in about 3 s:
  - server, board and BIOS from DMI (vendor placeholders dropped)
  - CPU sockets, cores, threads and NUMA nodes (`lscpu`); frequency driver, boost, max clock, EPP and idle states
  - usable and installed memory and populated channels (EDAC); DIMM model with rated and configured speed (udev's DMI records)
  - per GPU, from the amdgpu sysfs files every Slurm step can read: memory, power cap (and its default when lowered), compute/memory partition, perf level and max sclk, VBIOS, PCIe link
  - host GPU driver release from the `amdgpu-dkms` package (deb or rpm; `…30100100` is 30.10.1), and the ROCm release of the host's repo.radeon.com repository
  - active RDMA ports with driver, rate and firmware; OS, kernel and kernel command line
- `batch_host_<stamp>.txt` has each node's values as `key: value` lines. After them comes the raw data: `lscpu`, `numactl -H`, idle states, DIMMs, per-GPU sysfs, RDMA ports, amdgpu module parameters, driver packages and repositories, Docker and network interfaces.
- The batch summary carries the one-line `System`. Every run banner carries it too, plus the fields behind it: server, BIOS, OS, kernel and command line, CPU topology, frequency and idle states, host memory, GPU VRAM, power cap, partition, clocks, VBIOS and PCIe, host GPU driver and package, RDMA NICs.
- Multi-node: `Host check` says whether every node reported the same platform. If not, the summary warns with the keys that differ, and the end of `batch_host_<stamp>.txt` lists each value with how many nodes had it. When the runner is not one of the nodes (e.g. salloc on a login node), the first node's platform is used.
- The GPU's marketing name and memory type come from amd-smi on the runner. Without it, the sysfs product name is used and the memory type is left out.
### Extraction and report (`extract_results.py` parser versions 5 and 6, `report.py`)
- 19 platform columns: `system_description`, `host_check`, `server`, `bios`, `os`, `kernel`, `kernel_cmdline`, `cpu_*`, `host_memory`, `gpu_*`, `rdma_nics`. They are appended, so readers that index columns by position keep working.
- Overview: the Hardware section shows the system description and every platform field per batch. Runs: a new System column.
### Fixes
- **TorchTitan TFLOP/s at or above 1,000.** TorchTitan prints `tflops: {tflops:,.2f}`. The pattern stopped at the comma, so `1,293.62` became 1. For llama3.1 8B/70B BF16/FP8 on MI355X, the reported value goes from 1.0 to between 1208.9 and 1701.5.
- **Megatron-Bridge post-training.** `MODEL_TFLOP/s/GPU` is an estimate: global batch × `seq_length` × FLOPs per token, divided by step time. Without packed sequences, post-training pads each micro-batch only to its longest sample, a few hundred tokens for SQuAD against a `seq_length` of 8192. So the Qwen3-32B LoRA recipe reported 13,987 TFLOP/s/GPU, about 5.6× MI355X's BF16 peak. For these runs (`post_trainer`, `packed_sequence` resolved to false, Megatron-Bridge's default):
  - the estimate is kept as `hmean_nominal_tflops` ("Nominal TFLOP/s per GPU" in the report), and `hmean_tflops` is empty
  - throughput is samples/s/GPU, from each iteration's global batch size and step time
  - `throughput_note` says why
  Pretraining and packed post-training keep their TFLOP/s.
- The Performance sheet drops its Notes column. "Runs ok / total" and the Runs sheet carry what it said.
## Behaviour changes to note
- Existing result directories: run `extract_results.py <dir>`, then `report.py`, to pick up the two fixes. `report.py` already re-parses a `results.json` from an older parser version, without writing it.
- Megatron-Bridge SFT/LoRA rows without packed sequences no longer have TFLOP/s. Compare them on nominal TFLOP/s or samples/s/GPU, within one config.
- Run banners are about 20 lines longer: 77 lines on MI355X, within the extractor's 200-line banner window.
- The Performance sheet has no Notes column.

+###############################################################################
+# Copyright (c) 2026, Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. All rights reserved.
+#
+# See LICENSE for license information.
+###############################################################################
+
+"""Unit tests for the platform capture in tools/perf/lib/common.sh.
+
+The perf_host_* functions run on every node of a batch and feed the system
+description that results are quoted with, so these pin down its wording, the
+host GPU driver decoding and the multi-node comparison. The library is
+sourced under the runners' shell options (set -uo pipefail, nullglob) with
+stdin held open, so an unset variable or a command left reading stdin fails
+here instead of hanging a batch.
+
+Pure CPU; needs bash, no GPU and no root.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import os
+import re
+import shutil
+import socket
+import subprocess
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pytest
+
+REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
+LIB = REPO_ROOT / "tools" / "perf" / "lib"
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(shutil.which("bash") is None, reason="needs bash")
+
+
+def bash(script: str, timeout: int = 120) -> str:
+    """Run ``script`` after sourcing lib/common.sh and lib/control.sh."""
+    read_end, write_end = os.pipe()
+    try:
+        out = subprocess.run(
+            [
+                "bash",
+                "-c",
+                f"set -uo pipefail\nshopt -s nullglob\nsource {LIB}/common.sh\n"
+                f"PERF_MULTINODE=${{PERF_MULTINODE:-0}}\nsource {LIB}/control.sh\n{script}",
+            ],
+            stdin=read_end,
+            capture_output=True,
+            text=True,
+            timeout=timeout,
+            env={**os.environ, "PRIMUS_PATH": str(REPO_ROOT)},
+            check=False,
+        )
+    finally:
+        os.close(read_end)
+        os.close(write_end)
+    assert out.returncode == 0, out.stderr
+    assert "unbound variable" not in out.stderr, out.stderr
+    return out.stdout
+
+
+# Every key the banner reads.
+SETTINGS_KEYS = (
+    "cpu_governor numa_balancing transparent_hugepages thp_defrag iommu amdgpu_driver kernel cpu_model "
+    "cpus memory os kernel_cmdline server board bios cpu_sockets cpu_cores_per_socket cpu_threads_per_core "
+    "numa_nodes cpu_frequency cpu_idle memory_installed memory_dimms rdma_nics gpu_count gpu_product "
+    "gpu_vram gpu_power_cap gpu_partition gpu_clocks gpu_vbios gpu_pcie gpu_driver gpu_driver_package"
+).split()
+
+MI355X_SETTINGS = """\
+cpu_governor: schedutil x256
+amdgpu_driver: 6.14.14
+cpu_model: AMD EPYC 9575F 64-Core Processor
+cpus: 256
+memory: 3023 GiB
+os: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS
+server: Supermicro AS -4126GS-NMR-LCC
+bios: 1.7 (09/12/2025, American Megatrends International, LLC.)
+cpu_sockets: 2
+cpu_cores_per_socket: 64
+cpu_threads_per_core: 2
+numa_nodes: 2
+memory_installed: 3072 GiB Registered-DDR5, 24 channels
+memory_dimms: 128 GiB Samsung M321RAJA0MB2-CCPWF, 6400 MT/s, configured 6000 MT/s
+gpu_count: 8
+gpu_product: AMD Instinct MI355 OAM
+gpu_vram: 288 GiB
+gpu_power_cap: 1400 W
+gpu_driver: amdgpu 30.10.1 (ROCm 7.0.1)
+"""
+
+
+def describe(settings: str, gpu_model: str = "AMD Instinct MI355X", vram_type: str = "HBM3E") -> str:
+    """perf_system_description for canned settings, with amd-smi's answers stubbed."""
+    return bash(
+        f"PERF_HOST_SETTINGS=$(cat <<'EOF'\n{settings}EOF\n)\n"
+        f"perf_gpu_model() {{ echo '{gpu_model}'; }}\n"
+        f"perf_gpu_vram_type() {{ printf '%s' '{vram_type}'; }}\n"
+        "perf_system_description\n"
+    ).strip()
+
+
+def test_system_description_reads_like_a_results_footnote():
+    assert describe(MI355X_SETTINGS) == (
+        "Dual AMD EPYC 9575F 64-Core Processor-based Supermicro AS -4126GS-NMR-LCC server with "
+        "8x AMD Instinct MI355X (288GB HBM3E 1400W) GPUs, 1 NUMA node per socket, System BIOS 1.7, "
+        "Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, Host GPU driver amdgpu 30.10.1 (ROCm 7.0.1)"
+    )
+
+
+def test_system_description_leaves_out_what_is_unknown():
+    settings = (
+        MI355X_SETTINGS.replace("cpu_sockets: 2", "cpu_sockets: 1")
+        .replace("numa_nodes: 2", "numa_nodes: 4")
+        .replace("bios: 1.7 (09/12/2025, American Megatrends International, LLC.)", "bios: unknown (Vultr)")
+        .replace("server: Supermicro AS -4126GS-NMR-LCC", "server: unknown")
+        .replace("gpu_power_cap: 1400 W", "gpu_power_cap: 1400 W x7, 1000 W x1")
+    )
+    # amd-smi sees no GPU (a Slurm step without them): sysfs' product name,
+    # and no memory type.
+    assert describe(settings, gpu_model="unknown", vram_type="") == (
+        "Single AMD EPYC 9575F 64-Core Processor-based server with 8x AMD Instinct MI355 OAM "
+        "(288GB 1400 W x7, 1000 W x1) GPUs, 4 NUMA nodes per socket, Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, "
+        "Host GPU driver amdgpu 30.10.1 (ROCm 7.0.1)"
+    )
+
+
+def test_system_description_without_gpus():
+    settings = re.sub(r"(?m)^gpu_.*\n", "", MI355X_SETTINGS) + "gpu_count: 0\ngpu_driver: not loaded\n"
+    assert describe(settings) == (
+        "Dual AMD EPYC 9575F 64-Core Processor-based Supermicro AS -4126GS-NMR-LCC server, "
+        "1 NUMA node per socket, System BIOS 1.7, Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS"
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "package,rocm,expected",
+    [
+        ("1:6.14.14.30100100-2212064.22.04", "7.0.1", "amdgpu 30.10.1 (ROCm 7.0.1)"),
+        ("1:6.14.14.30100101-2212064.22.04", "", "amdgpu 30.10.1.1"),
+        # rpm: no epoch.
+        ("6.16.6.30200000-2238411.el9", "7.1.0", "amdgpu 30.20.0 (ROCm 7.1.0)"),
+        # Before the 30.x numbering the release was ROCm's.
+        ("1:6.10.5.60401-2164967.22.04", "6.4.1", "ROCm 6.4.1"),
+        ("1:6.10.5-custom", "", "amdgpu-dkms 1:6.10.5-custom"),
+    ],
+)
+def test_host_gpu_driver_from_its_package(package, rocm, expected):
+    assert bash(f"perf_host_gpu_driver '{package}' '{rocm}'").strip() == expected
+
+
+def test_tally_names_the_most_common_value_first():
+    assert bash("printf 'a\\nb\\na\\n\\n' | perf_host_tally").strip() == "a x2, b x1"
+    assert bash("printf 'a\\na\\n' | perf_host_tally").strip() == "a"
+    assert bash("printf '' | perf_host_tally") == ""
+    assert bash("perf_host_field gpu_vram ''").strip() == "gpu_vram: unknown"
+
+
+def test_this_hosts_settings_are_one_key_value_per_line():
+    lines = bash("perf_host_settings").splitlines()
+    keys = []
+    for line in lines:
+        m = re.match(r"^([a-z_]+): (.*)$", line)
+        assert m, f"not a 'key: value' line: {line!r}"
+        keys.append(m.group(1))
+    assert len(keys) == len(set(keys)), "duplicate keys"
+    assert set(SETTINGS_KEYS) <= set(keys), set(SETTINGS_KEYS) - set(keys)
+
+
+def test_snapshot_section_is_the_settings_and_details_follow(tmp_path):
+    snapshot, settings = tmp_path / "batch_host.txt", tmp_path / "settings.txt"
+    bash(f"perf_host_snapshot > {snapshot}\nperf_host_settings > {settings}\n")
+    section = bash(f'perf_host_section {snapshot} "$(hostname)"')
+    assert section == settings.read_text()
+    text = snapshot.read_text()
+    assert text.startswith(f"== {socket.gethostname()} ==\n")
+    for name in (
+        "lscpu",
+        "numa",
+        "memory",
+        "gpus (sysfs)",
+        "rdma",
+        "driver packages and repositories",
+        "interfaces",
+    ):
+        assert f"\n-- {name} --\n" in text, name
+
+
+SNAPSHOT = """\
+== node-a ==
+bios: 1.7
+gpu_power_cap: 1400 W
+-- lscpu --
+CPU MHz: 1500
+== node-b ==
+bios: 1.8
+gpu_power_cap: 1400 W
